dedupe_keys.name: compartment fire temperatures from body worn and platform mounted sensors in live fire suppression exercises uk and us

description: This dataset records temperatures inside burning compartments during live fire-suppression training exercises at fire training facilities in the United Kingdom and the United States. It was deposited on Mendeley Data by Syed Yusuf in October 2019. Temperature monitoring devices were worn on the breathing apparatus harnesses of instructors or fixed to stands at 1.3 and 1.7 metres, and logged time-stamped values in degrees Celsius. Sessions included a gas cooling demonstration in a lay-flat chamber, a re-qualification exercise in a multi-compartment chamber and exercises in an industrial building following standard operating procedures, and the description explains which device was where in each session. The files are free to download online under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: the data come from a few training sessions with training fuels, device positions changed between sessions, and file formats are not listed in the metadata. Simulation uses: thermal exposure profiles for firefighter protective equipment and fire service operations models. Related records: the NIOSH firefighter anthropometry data (data-niosh-firefighter-anthropometry) and the NFPA fatality reports (data-nfpa-fatal-firefighter-injuries-united-states) cover other responder safety aspects.
